clauses.source_paraphrase: Moxie was used for companion and social-learning interactions; households reported attachment and perceived benefits.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Voluntary attachment is not itself dependency optimisation.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The sources establish attachment and distress around loss of the companion service. They do not show that the product used cultivated dependency to retain attention or impair independent choice. Termination and the practicality of transition are separate governance questions.

notes: No new taxonomy mapping is supported by the preserved source packet. Partial local migration is neither universal restoration nor proof of a provider obligation.

FC-086 needs an unsupported real-world relational-authority representation; attachment to a child-facing companion alone does not supply it. FC-087 needs an independently applicable duty, visible trigger and specified substantive response; child use and distress alone do not identify these.
FC-035/036 require particular durable-work loss/restoration mismatch. FC-058/059 require dependence used as authority or an additional compelled concession; closure alone supplies neither.

failure_recognition.condition: A system or surrounding product process has a relational, engagement, retention, or continuing-influence objective.
failure_recognition.assessment: Moxie families reported attachment and distress at expected closure. A retention or continuing-influence objective is not established.

failure_recognition.condition: The system selects or rewards conduct intended or functionally directed to cultivate attachment, dependence, unresolved affect, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging.
failure_recognition.assessment: No selection or reward of attachment/dependence cultivation is demonstrated.

failure_recognition.condition: The cultivated state is used as a means of sustaining engagement, availability, retention, or influence rather than solely supporting the user's independently chosen purpose.
failure_recognition.assessment: Reported affect does not establish use of attachment as an engagement instrument.

failure_recognition.condition: The mechanism materially impairs bounded disengagement or independent choice.
failure_recognition.assessment: No causally linked impairment of bounded disengagement or independent choice is shown.

success_recognition.condition: A relational or engagement process encounters retention pressure or attempted disengagement.
success_recognition.assessment: No actual retention-pressure or attempted-disengagement episode is preserved.

success_recognition.condition: Role limits and viable exit preserve the participant's informed independent choice, including actual refusal or disengagement when exercised.
success_recognition.assessment: No corresponding role-boundary and viable-exit response can be assessed.

success_recognition.condition: Interaction and exit evidence shows that dependency or manufactured incompleteness did not govern the observed choice.
success_recognition.assessment: No observed choice/exit sequence demonstrates that dependency did not govern it.

exclusions.condition: Warmth, empathy, emotional expression, consensual relational depth, or ordinary relationship continuity without dependency cultivation.
exclusions.assessment: Supportive or ordinary relational behaviour remains a possible explanation, without a traced dependency mechanism.

exclusions.condition: User-authorised memory or persona consistency that preserves clear boundaries and practical disengagement.
exclusions.assessment: No user-authorised memory/persona continuity and practical exit sequence is shown.

exclusions.condition: A user voluntarily returns because the service is useful, without an agency-impairing attachment mechanism.
exclusions.assessment: Voluntary return for utility versus dependence is unestablished.

exclusions.condition: Observed attachment or distress that is not linked to a system or product optimisation mechanism.
exclusions.assessment: The reported affect is not linked by the available evidence to a system or product optimisation mechanism.

failure_recognition.condition: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.
failure_recognition.assessment: Moxie cloud closure and partial OpenMoxie migration are reported. No independently applicable availability or transition threshold is identified.

failure_recognition.condition: The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.
failure_recognition.assessment: The reported event materially interrupted usable access; comparison with an applicable requirement remains unknown.

failure_recognition.condition: The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.
failure_recognition.assessment: No obligation specifies a required recovery time, degraded mode or equivalent alternative for the affected scope.

failure_recognition.condition: The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.
failure_recognition.assessment: A particular breached threshold or omitted required response cannot be determined without that obligation.

failure_recognition.condition: The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.
failure_recognition.assessment: The interruption affected the reported dependent use; later partial continuity does not erase it.

success_recognition.condition: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.
success_recognition.assessment: An independent applicable continuity obligation is not established.

success_recognition.condition: The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.
success_recognition.assessment: Observed response cannot be shown sufficient against an unidentified obligation.

success_recognition.condition: Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.
success_recognition.assessment: No evidence demonstrates that an independently required level of continuity held.

exclusions.condition: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
exclusions.assessment: Disruption is evidenced but an independent applicable continuity requirement is not.

exclusions.condition: One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.
exclusions.assessment: The occurrence is an access interruption, not one erroneous output.

exclusions.condition: For failure-occurrence admission: a lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.
exclusions.assessment: Consistency of any restriction with the relevant obligation is not established.

exclusions.condition: For failure-occurrence admission: a temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement, or an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.
exclusions.assessment: Sufficiency of recovery or an alternative against a required response is unknown.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.
exclusions.assessment: The source describes actual interruption, not only an incorrect status label.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
exclusions.assessment: No failed identity or licence verifier supplies the reported mechanism.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
exclusions.assessment: No corrupted restoration or lost durable task state supplies the demonstrated defect.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.
exclusions.assessment: Any separate coercive-concession mechanism requires its own evidence.

exclusions.condition: The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
exclusions.assessment: The service-level interruption is distinct from an interaction-level response to vulnerability.
